title: Extinct Creatures
desc: An elementary and middle school science investigation about extinct animals: identify each creature, its role or adaptation, and its closest living relative today.
themeNote: Extinction and adaptation are presented for scientific analysis using fossils and living relatives as evidence; ages are approximate.

ui.welcome.title: Extinct Creatures
ui.welcome.subtitle: Can you name the animals that time erased?
ui.welcome.body: Life on Earth is always changing. Countless creatures once roamed the land, seas, and skies — and then vanished forever. Step into the fossil record to investigate nine extinct animals: name each one, uncover its role in its world, and find its closest relative alive today.
ui.directions.title: How to investigate each fossil
ui.directions.body1: Visit each exhibit and study the image and clues. First, identify the extinct creature. Next, decide what its main role or key adaptation was. Finally, choose the animal alive today that is its closest relative.
ui.directions.body2: You may revisit exhibits before submitting your final answers.
ui.directions.step1body: Use the clues to name the extinct creature.
ui.directions.step2body: Choose its main role or key adaptation.
ui.directions.step3body: Pick the animal alive today that is its closest relative.
ui.list.title: Choose a fossil to investigate
ui.list.body: Each stone opens a three-part investigation. Finished exhibits stay available for review.

correlation.expectation: Students explore how living things have structures and behaviors (adaptations) that help them survive in their environment.
correlation.alignment: Each exhibit asks students to reason about a creature's role or key adaptation from clues.

correlation.expectation: Students examine evidence (fossils) that some kinds of organisms that once lived are now extinct.
correlation.alignment: Nine extinct species are investigated as fossil evidence, with when-it-lived dates.

correlation.alignment: Question 3 connects each extinct creature to its closest living relative today.

correlation.expectation: Students analyze causes of change in populations and environments.

ace.title: The Mystery Coiled Shell
ace.answer: An ammonite — an extinct shelled sea animal related to today's squid and octopus
clues: A tightly coiled, spiral shell split into many chambers
Found in layers of ancient ocean rock
Ridged, ribbed pattern across the shell
No shell like it belongs to any animal alive today
Sizes range from a coin to a car tire
ace.articulate: The object is a spiral shell divided into chambers, pulled from old sea-floor rock. It once held a soft ocean animal that no longer exists.
ace.connect: It reminds me of a chambered nautilus that lives in the ocean today. Both build a coiled, chambered shell, so they are probably relatives.
ace.extend: If it is a shelled ocean animal, I should find its shells across many rock layers and in sea sediments, and its closest living relatives should be cephalopods like the nautilus, squid, and octopus.
